Short impact summary

This Zenodo software release for JaneliaSciComp/workstation shows early but tangible uptake: it has 303 downloads, 691 views, and 2 OpenAlex citations. The record also captures 2 downstream reuse events, indicating that the release is being incorporated into scholarly work rather than only accessed.

Full narrative

JaneliaSciComp/workstation 9.20.1 is an openly available software release deposited in Zenodo and linked to a GitHub software version, which supports transparent stewardship and versioned reuse. The usage record is the clearest signal of reach so far, with substantially more views than downloads and enough activity to suggest that the release is being discovered and considered by users.

Scholarly uptake is still early, but it is visible. OpenAlex attributes 2 citations to this release, and the reuse graph also identifies 2 documented downstream reuses, both in articles/preprints. Taken together, these signals show that the software is already part of the research workflow around the work it accompanies, even though the citation base remains small.

The citing literature is concentrated in eLife and sits within neurobiology and insect physiology research, especially work on Drosophila resources. That pattern suggests the workstation release is being used in the context of data-rich life science studies rather than spreading broadly across many fields at this stage.

There is little public-discourse evidence in the available record, so the story here is primarily one of usage and scholarly incorporation rather than media attention. Overall, the release appears to have an active early footprint: steady access, a small but real citation trail, and documented reuse in related research outputs.
